title: Relay message model v2
description: The canonical wire contract for Relay's message model: one send is one message, every stored part carries a permanent identity, replies target parts, reactions are scoped, and edits are versioned part operations. Relay-Server owns this file. Every shape here is generated from and validated against real server responses by server/scripts/contract-fixtures-test.ts; nothing may be added to it that the server does not emit.
$comment: Clients MUST tolerate part types they do not know. The Part union is deliberately open: an unrecognised `type` matches $defs/UnknownPart, which requires only the identity fields (part_id, part_index, position) and permits any other member. Render such a part with the message's fallback_text and leave it otherwise untouched — do not drop it, and do not fail the message. Clients MUST also tolerate additive members on known shapes: Relay adds optional fields without a version bump.

messageId.description: A client-generated message identity. Lowercase Crockford base32 ULID; the client mints it before queueing the send and it is both the canonical id and the send's idempotency key.

partId.description: A permanent part identity. Survives edits, reordering and removal; a removed part keeps its id as a tombstone so a reply that targeted it still resolves to the right thing.

operationId.description: A client-generated mutation identity: one per logical edit, unsend or reaction change. Retrying with the same id and the same request replays the original result; the same id with a different request is a 409 idempotency_conflict.

MentionRange.description: One inline mention over a text part. `start` and `length` are UTF-16 code-unit offsets into that part's `text`, which contains the display name the sender inserted and never an '@'.

StyleRange.description: One formatting run over a text part, in the same UTF-16 offsets mentions use. Presentation only: the text stays canonical and fallback text ignores styling.

styles.description: An empty array is meaningful: it marks structured plain text, distinguishing it from a legacy Markdown body. Absent means legacy.

blurHash.description: Compact placeholder a client decodes into a soft preview before the bytes download.

MediaPart.description: A photo, video, audio file or document. Attachment-backed media carries `attachment_id` and a capability `url`; remote media carries `url` alone.

LinkPreviewPart.description: Metadata the SENDER resolved, carried with the message, so a recipient never opens a connection to a URL somebody else chose. `title` and `description` may be absent while the sender-side unfurl is still resolving.

DataPart.description: A structured component. `data.type` names the component; see schemas/parts/ for the published component shapes.

UnknownPart.description: The catch-all that keeps the Part union open. A client that meets a part type it does not know MUST render the message's fallback_text for it rather than dropping the part or rejecting the message. `poll` parts land here for clients written before the poll surface shipped.

Part.description: One part of a message, discriminated on `type`. The union is open by design; see UnknownPart.

ReplyQuote.description: A snapshot of the target taken when the reply was committed, frozen thereafter. It is never re-resolved: editing the target does not rewrite the quote, and losing the target redacts it rather than repointing it.

target_kind.description: The stored kind of the quoted part, which is finer-grained than the wire `type`: a contact card and a group-invite card both project as a `data` part but quote as their own kind.

oneOf.description: The reply edge as one viewer sees it. `message_id` and `part_id` are permanent; `quote_state` and `quote` are what changed since.

part_id.description: Present when the reply targeted one specific part. It keeps pointing at that part's identity even after the part is removed, so a reply to the middle photo never silently becomes a reply to a different photo.

quote_state.description: active: the quote below is live. unsent: the sender unsent the target. part_removed: an edit removed the quoted part. moderated / redacted: Relay removed the content. unavailable: this viewer's membership window does not include the target, so the edge is visible but its content is not.

Reaction.description: One reaction as projected onto a message. One per (message, target slot, actor): adding a second emoji to the same slot replaces the first.

part_index.description: The target part's CURRENT position, derived at read time from the live parts; null for a message-scoped reaction. Retained for clients that key reaction slots by index, and never authority — target_part_id is.

actor_kind.description: The published actor kind. Storage spells an agent `contact`; the wire never does.

ReceiptSummary.description: How many eligible recipients reached each state, so `read` is never mistaken for 'everyone read'.

Revision.description: A prior version of a message, oldest first. The current version is never in this list. An unsent message's revisions are redacted along with everything else.

replaced_at.description: When the next version replaced it.

EditCapabilities.description: The server's answer to 'what can this viewer do to this message right now'. Clients hide controls this says are unavailable rather than deriving the policy themselves. `editable_parts` is empty when can_edit is false.

VisibleMessage.description: A message that still has content. `reactions`, `revisions`, `receipt_summary` and `edit_capabilities` are resolved on reads and on the edit response; a send response carries the committed message alone.

is_from_me.description: True when the authenticated account this payload was projected for is the sender. Relay resolves direction so a client never compares sender.id against its own identity — a comparison that is wrong for every other human in a group.

fallback_text.description: A plain-text rendering of the whole message, for notifications, previews and any client that cannot render a part it was handed.

version.description: The current version number. 1 for a never-edited message; five successful edits is the ceiling, so 6 is the highest value.

Tombstone.description: What is left after an unsend: the identity, the place in the conversation, and who sent it. No parts, no fallback text, no reactions, no revisions — a tombstone that exposed parts would defeat the unsend.

is_from_me.description: Kept on the tombstone because it is all that is left to say whether the client renders "You unsent a message" or names the other participant.

unsent_at.description: Present iff the sender unsent the message; absent for moderation or other deletion.

IncomingPart.description: A part as a client submits it. The server mints the identity; a client never supplies part_id, part_index or position.

PartOperation.description: One step of an edit. Operations apply in array order against the version named by expected_version. Which actions a part accepts is per kind and is published on the message as edit_capabilities: text updates in place; media and voice memos are removed, moved or replaced (never rewritten, because the bytes are a different identity); link previews and data components move or go.

position.description: Where the new part lands. Appended when omitted.

oneOf.description: Replace tombstones the old identity and mints a new one; reactions on the replaced part go with it.

SendRequestV2.description: POST /v2/conversations/{conversation_id}/messages. One send is one message: mixed media and text stay together instead of being split into a run of messages. `message_id` is the idempotency key — retrying the same id with the same request replays the original 201.

reply_to.description: v2 accepts a stable part id only. The legacy `part_index` form is rejected with a 422.

invocation_id.description: Agent senders only: the invocation this message answers.

SendResponseV2.$comment: 201. A replayed send whose message has since been unsent answers with the tombstone, never the content, which is why this is Message and not VisibleMessage.

EditRequestV2.description: PATCH /v2/messages/{message_id}. `expected_version` is optimistic concurrency: two devices editing version 2 produce exactly one version 3 and the loser gets a 409.

UnsendRequestV2.description: DELETE /v2/messages/{message_id}. The operation id may also travel as an Idempotency-Key header when it is itself a mut_ id.

ReactionRequest.description: POST /v1/messages/{message_id}/reactions. Omit both target fields to react to the whole message.

target_part_id.description: Required when target_scope is `part`; supplying it alone implies part scope. Targets any part kind.

part_index.description: DEPRECATED legacy input. Translated to the target's live part id at the boundary and never stored. It keeps its original media-only rule: an index naming a non-media part is a 422. Use target_part_id.

ReactionResult.description: Both the 200 body and the reaction.added / reaction.removed event payload, which is why it carries the published actor shape rather than the projected one.

changed.description: False when the request was a no-op — removing a reaction that was not there, or re-adding the one already in the slot. Events are emitted only when this is true.

ErrorBody.description: Every Relay error. `idempotency_conflict` is a 409 and means the operation id was reused with a different request, or the original is still in flight — in which case a Retry-After header names the wait.
